methods.name: Peer-Median

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Equilibrium Energy is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Ryan Hanley and Alvin Henrick that has raised $103M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of nine private and one public company operating in Climate & Energy, including same-stage peers KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach applied a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $103M total raised proxy, implying a $196M valuation. The peer-median method benchmarked against three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.0B and a range spanning $700M to $3.0B, directly implying $1.0B. These methods were selected as most applicable given available capital and peer transaction data; comparable revenue and margin multiples were not available for this stage.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $166M to $1.1B, with a median point of $598M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around: (1) which peer cohort most accurately reflects Equilibrium's competitive positioning and technology maturity, (2) whether stage-progression or peer-based methods better capture frontier-energy risk premia, and (3) underlying variance in peer valuations ($3.0B range across the three comps). A more precise view would require additional granularity on unit economics and technology validation metrics.
